title: Chyme sampling from the digestive tract of Octopus maya
author: Daisy Pineda-Suazo
materials: Ensure all tools and equipment are clean and sterilized before starting.
Prepare the workspace with necessary materials, ensuring easy access to surgical instruments, centrifuge, liquid nitrogen, and Eppendorf tubes.
Use proper personal protective equipment (PPE) throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Dissect and isolate digestive sections
steps.instruction: Carefully dissect the digestive tract of Octopus maya, identify and separate the anterior salivary glands (BM), crop (Cr), stomach (St), caecum (Ca), and digestive gland (DG), and use surgical clamps to isolate each section, preventing mixing of digestive contents between sections.

steps.title: Open sections and transfer chyme
steps.instruction: Open each isolated section carefully to access the chyme and transfer the chyme into labeled Eppendorf tubes.

steps.title: Centrifuge chyme samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the chyme samples at 13370 × g, °C, for 5 minutes to separate solids from the supernatant.

steps.title: Freeze and store supernatant
steps.instruction: Collect the supernatant, freeze it immediately in liquid nitrogen, and store the frozen samples at –40 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Homogenize gland tissue
steps.instruction: Liquefy and homogenize the glands using a tissue homogenizer (e.g., ULTRA‑TURRAX IKA T18 basic) at an appropriate speed for uniform homogenization.

steps.title: Transfer and centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenized sample into an Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 13370 × g, °C, for 5 minutes to obtain a clear supernatant.

steps.title: Freeze gland supernatant
steps.instruction: Freeze the supernatant in liquid nitrogen immediately after centrifugation.

description: Store the sample at -40 °C until further analysis. Notes and precautions: Ensure the surgical clamps are properly placed to prevent cross-contamination of digestive contents. Work quickly when handling biological samples to preserve enzyme activity. Properly label all tubes with the section of the digestive tract and the sample type for accurate identification. Use liquid nitrogen with caution and follow appropriate safety protocols to avoid burns or injuries. Storage: Samples should remain frozen at -40 °C to preserve enzyme and metabolite integrity until the time of analysis.
